report.headline: Usage projected to rise to 22.8% in the EuroLeague from an already below-average 18.3% NBA usage rate, but the shooting-efficiency projection is not trustworthy here.

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 22.8% in the EuroLeague, up from 18.3% in the source NBA season, with an 80% interval of 18.7%-27.0% and a 95% interval of 16.5%-29.2%, against a EuroLeague mean of 20.3% and standard deviation of 4.2%.

risks.text: The subject's NBA usage rate (18.3%) and true shooting percentage (52.2%) were both below league average, at -0.34 and -0.37 standard deviations respectively, in the source season.

Players who historically made this NBA-to-EuroLeague move averaged -0.31 standard deviations relative to their own league, meaning this cohort itself skews below-average rather than star-level, which limits how much the projection should be read as a breakout.
The true shooting projection of 56.6% is unsupported: the model underperforms a simple league-mean guess on this metric (4.7% error either way), so no efficiency conclusion should be drawn from it.

The 95% interval for usage rate spans 16.5% to 29.2%, nearly the full range of common EuroLeague roles, reflecting substantial individual-level uncertainty despite a two-season gap since the source season.

strengths.text: The subject posted a 16.7% assist rate alongside 3.816 assists per 75 possessions in the source NBA season, indicating playmaking production even in a limited role.
Turnover rate was a low 12.1% in the source season, suggesting efficient ball-handling relative to usage.
62.8% of the subject's shot attempts came from three, a profile that projects to translate well to a floor-spacing role.
The model's usage projection beats a trivial league-mean baseline, so the projected role increase to 22.8% usage is a genuine signal rather than noise.

uncertainty.text: The usage projection is informative — its 3.3% mean absolute error beats the 4.3% error of the league-mean baseline over 367 held-out transitions — but its 80% interval still spans roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, so it can rank this player but not pin down a single number. The true-shooting projection of 56.6% cannot be trusted at all: its 4.7% mean absolute error is no better than the 4.7% error of simply guessing the league-mean true shooting percentage, so that number carries no real information.
